title: Expected number within a distance of the mean
source: Theory S1-8.3 Quick check 1; P(mod(X - mu) < d) = 2 Phi(z) - 1, expected number = n p
stem: The random variable \(X\) has the distribution \(\mathrm{N}({mu|int}, {s|int}^2)\). A random sample of \({n|int}\) values of \(X\) is taken. Given that \(\Phi({Z|raw})={PH|raw}\), find the expected number of these values that lie within \({d|raw}\) of the mean, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

steps.name: Z
steps.note: Standardise the distance from the mean.

steps.name: P
steps.note: Use the symmetry of the normal curve: 2Φ(z) − 1.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Multiply the probability by the sample size.

contexts.note: Includes the original N(25, 4^2), sample of 500, within 4 of the mean, 341 (3 s.f.)

contexts.stem: The lengths of metal rods are normally distributed with mean \({mu|int}\) cm and standard deviation \({s|int}\) cm. A random sample of \({n|int}\) rods is chosen. Given that \(\Phi({Z|raw})={PH|raw}\), find the expected number of rods in the sample whose length is within \({d|raw}\) cm of the mean, correct to 3 significant figures.

The volume of juice in a bottle is normally distributed with mean \({mu|int}\) ml and standard deviation \({s|int}\) ml. In a batch of \({n|int}\) bottles, how many would you expect to contain a volume that differs from the mean by less than \({d|raw}\) ml? Use \(\Phi({Z|raw})={PH|raw}\) and give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

title: A normal probability inside a binomial probability
source: Theory S1-8.3 Quick check 2; p = P(X > x), then P(exactly one of m) = m p (1 - p)^(m - 1)
stem: The random variable \(X\) has the distribution \(\mathrm{N}({mu|int}, {s|int}^2)\). Given that \(\Phi({Z|raw})={PH|raw}\), find the probability that, of \({m|int}\) independent values of \(X\), exactly one is greater than \({x|raw}\).

steps.name: p
steps.note: Standardise and use the upper tail.

steps.name: K
steps.note: Binomial probability with m trials: m p (1 − p)^(m − 1).

contexts.note: Includes the original N(50, 5^2), 3 values, exactly one greater than 55, 0.337

contexts.stem: The volume of paint in a tin is normally distributed with mean \({mu|int}\) ml and standard deviation \({s|int}\) ml. \({m|int}\) tins are chosen at random. Using \(\Phi({Z|raw})={PH|raw}\), find the probability that exactly one of them contains more than \({x|raw}\) ml.

The times taken by runners to complete a course are normally distributed with mean \({mu|int}\) minutes and standard deviation \({s|int}\) minutes. Given that \(\Phi({Z|raw})={PH|raw}\), find the probability that exactly one of \({m|int}\) randomly chosen runners takes longer than \({x|raw}\) minutes.

title: Standard deviation from an observed count
source: Theory S1-8.3 Quick check 3; c/N = P(X > x) gives z, then (x - mu)/sigma = z
stem: The values of a variable are normally distributed with mean \({mu|int}\) and standard deviation \(\sigma\). In a random sample of \({N|int}\) values, \({c|int}\) were greater than \({x|int}\). Given that \(\Phi({Z|raw})={PH|raw}\), estimate \(\sigma\).

steps.name: T
steps.note: Use the relative frequency as the probability and find z from the table.

steps.name: K
steps.note: Equate the standardised value to z.

contexts.note: Includes the original mean 40, 40 of 400 greater than 46, sigma = 4.68

contexts.stem: The masses, in grams, of bags of flour are normally distributed with mean \({mu|int}\) and standard deviation \(\sigma\). In a random sample of \({N|int}\) bags, \({c|int}\) weighed more than \({x|int}\) grams. Using \(\Phi({Z|raw})={PH|raw}\), estimate \(\sigma\).

The time, in minutes, that Lina spends reading each day is normally distributed with mean \({mu|int}\) and standard deviation \(\sigma\). Over \({N|int}\) days she read for more than \({x|int}\) minutes on \({c|int}\) days. Given that \(\Phi({Z|raw})={PH|raw}\), estimate \(\sigma\).

title: Expected number of rods within 0.5 cm of the mean

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
A company produces a particular type of metal rod. The lengths of these rods are normally distributed with mean 25.2 cm and standard deviation 0.4 cm. A random sample of 500 of these rods is chosen.

How many rods in this sample would you expect to have a length that is within 0.5 cm of the mean length? [5]

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: M1, use of ± standardisation formula once; no continuity correction, σ², √σ.

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: A1, for AWRT 0.8944 SOI.

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: M1, appropriate area 2Φ − 1 OE, from final process, must be probability.

steps.name: s5
steps.note: Official MS: B1FT, correct or FT their 4 s.f. (or better) probability; final answer must be a positive integer, not 394.0 or 395.0, only 1 answer.

title: Standard deviation from the number of heavy bags

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
The weights of bags of sugar are normally distributed with mean 1.04 kg and standard deviation \(\sigma\) kg. In a random sample of 2000 bags of sugar, 72 weighed more than 1.10 kg.

Find the value of \(\sigma\). [4]

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: B1, 1.79 < z ⩽ 1.80 (or −1.80 ⩽ z < −1.79) seen.

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: B1, 1.1 and 1.04 substituted in ± standardisation formula; allow continuity correction, not σ² or √σ.

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: M1, equate their ± standardisation formula to a z-value and solve for the appropriate area leading to final answer (expect σ < 0.5).

steps.name: s4
steps.note: Official MS: A1, 0.03335 ⩽ σ ⩽ 0.0334, at least 3 s.f.
